title: What If All the Ice on Earth Melted?

scenes.text: What if every glacier and ice sheet melted? The new map of Earth would shock you.
The sea would rise about two hundred feet, roughly sixty-five meters, once all that ice drained into the ocean.
Most of the ice sits on Antarctica and Greenland. Some scientists say melting it all would take over five thousand years.
Coastal cities would go under, and one estimate puts nearly three quarters of a billion people in Asia alone on the move.
The planet would also warm. An ice-free Earth would average about eighty degrees Fahrenheit, against fifty-eight today.
Not tonight, not this century. But the coastlines we know would be gone, redrawn over thousands of years.
